key_insight: The paper proposes a $C_4$-equivariant flow-matching generative model that learns polycrystalline microstructures as anisotropic power diagrams, enabling realistic synthesis at controllable resolution.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to generate synthetic microstructure data for materials design and property modeling when EBSD measurements are limited, costly, or time consuming.
method: Represents microstructures as anisotropic power-diagram graphs for a compact geometric encoding.
Trains a flow-matching graph neural network with $C_4$ rotational equivariance to preserve symmetry under 90° rotations.
Uses training-free guidance to steer generation toward target microstructure styles such as weld, cast, printed, and lamellar structures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative generation of several distinct real-world-like microstructure types and the ability to render samples at arbitrary pixel resolution.
watch_item: Performance is described mainly through generated examples in the abstract, so practical fidelity, diversity, and robustness will need validation on broader experimental datasets.
paper_title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
